To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the peripheral nerve injury-induced epigenetic reprogramming of gene expression is different from that of the spinal cord injury-induced epigenome.
“DNA methylation temporal profile following peripheral and central axotomy of the lumbar dorsal root axons is distinct and reveals a role for DNA methylation in the axonal regeneration program”.
DNA methylation temporal profile of DRG following peripheral and central axotomy shows a significant number of common and differentially regulated genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of epigenetic mechanisms involved in the axonal regenerating and non-regenerating phenotype.
the identification and characterization of the molecular pathways that are activated by axonal injury and the role of DNA epigenetic regulation in the axotomy-induced signaling cascade.
the epigenetic mechanisms of gene expression regulation and their role in neuronal phenotype determination.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this dataset provides an in-depth analysis of the DNA methylation changes in the axotomized DRG, allowing the identification of a set of genes whose methylation pattern may play a role in axonal regeneration.
DNA methylation profiling is a useful approach to identify genes and pathways associated with neuronal axonal regenerative and degenerative processes.
the DNA methylation profiling dataset presented in this article is a valuable resource for further investigation on axotomy-dependent pathways and the neuronal phenotype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the DNA methylation profile following peripheral axotomy is more dynamic and complex than that following central axotomy, and that this is consistent with the different regenerative potential of the respective axonal branches.
the DNA methylation temporal profiles in DRG following peripheral and central axotomies show distinct differences in methylation levels of the promoters and/or CpG islands of 5,000 genes.
the peripheral nerve axotomy induces a more pronounced and longer lasting DNA methylation reprograming than the central spinal axotomy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the axon regeneration program involves the activation of the DNA demethylation machinery, which in turn affects the expression of genes associated with the axonal regenerating phenotype.

the axotomy-dependent DNA methylation changes in DRG are more pronounced and more numerous following peripheral axotomy, which is consistent with the more robust regenerative response in the sciatic nerve.

DNA methylation profiling can be employed in a high throughput manner to assess the DNA methylation changes associated with axotomy, which can then be correlated to the axotomy-induced gene expression changes.
